 Oil India discovers natural gas in the Krishna Godavari basin
 Oil India discovers natural gas in Krishna-Godavari, where the Godavari-1 well recorded a peak flow rate of 200,000 SCMD. 
 By Moises Carrasquero on October 23, 2026 
 Table of Contents Oil India records peak flow of 200,000 SCMD at Godavari-1 
 The Matsyapuri training program is under evaluation 
 India's energy discovery and strategy 
 Oil India announced the discovery of natural gas in the Krishna-Godavari Basin, off the east coast of India. During testing of the Godavari-1 well, the company recorded a peak flow rate of 200,000 standard cubic meters per day (SCMD) of gas and a production of approximately 170 barrels per day of condensate.
 The discovery was made in a shallow water block awarded to the state-owned company during the Discovered Small Fields (DSF) bidding rounds. Currently, the company continues to assess the potential of the area to determine the development possibilities of the discovery.
 Oil India records peak flow of 200,000 SCMD at Godavari-1
 According to information published by Oil India, the discovery was made during testing of the Godavari-1 appraisal well, located in the offshore block KG-DSF/GSKW/2018. Testing operations began on October 16, 2026, in an interval with the presence of hydrocarbons, located at a depth of between 2,024 and 2,027 meters. During the appraisals, the well recorded a gas flow of approximately 100,000 SCMD, which reached a maximum of 200,000 SCMD in continuous testing.
 The company also reported condensate production of approximately 170 barrels per day. These results provide an initial indication of the behavior of the evaluated interval and offer information for continuing exploration efforts. However, the flow rates obtained during the tests alone do not allow for determining the total volume of recoverable resources or establishing the commercial viability of the discovery. For this, additional data on the characteristics of the reservoir and its production capacity will be necessary.
 The Matsyapuri training program is under evaluation
 The discovery is located in the Matsyapuri Formation, within the Krishna-Godavari Basin, off the east coast of India. According to the information consulted, this formation had not been previously evaluated in the area where the discovery was made, which adds to the significance of the results obtained by the company. As part of the next stages of evaluation, Oil India is preparing tests in a second, deeper interval. This work will allow for a broader understanding of the presence of hydrocarbons in the area and determine if there are favorable conditions to continue its development.
 To date, the company has not published an estimate of the resources associated with the discovery nor confirmed what volume of gas could be commercially recovered. Therefore, the current results constitute an initial reference point, pending further assessments. The performance of the second interval and the data obtained during the upcoming tests will be relevant for evaluating the block’s prospects. In particular, it will be necessary to determine whether the recorded flow rates can be maintained under production conditions and whether development is technically and economically viable.
 India’s energy discovery and strategy
 The discovery comes at a time when India is seeking to increase the share of natural gas in its energy mix and reduce its dependence on imports. According to data provided for this news report, the government aims to raise the proportion of gas in national energy consumption from 6 % to 15 % by 2030.
 In this scenario, domestic discoveries represent an opportunity to expand the availability of energy resources and strengthen domestic supply, however, their contribution will depend on factors such as the confirmation of recoverable resources, the economic viability of the project, and the availability of infrastructure to process and transport the gas to consumer markets.
 To Oil India the next step will be to complete testing of the deepest interval and gather additional information on the KG-DSF/GSKW/2018 block. The results will allow for further evaluation of the field and a more precise determination of its development prospects. Until the company publishes new estimates, the commercial potential of the discovery will remain undetermined. The upcoming assessments will be crucial in understanding the extent of the find and its potential contribution to India’s natural gas supply.
